Boles De Cidre Brut

Served at: Candlemas (Feast of the Presentation)

Serves 4Prep 20 minCook 40 min

Boles de Cidre Brut is a traditional French dish from Normandy, often enjoyed during Candlemas, the Feast of the Presentation. This hearty recipe features meatballs cooked in a dry cider sauce, symbolizing the region's rich apple harvest and the festive spirit of the holiday.

Ingredients

  • 1 lb (450 g) ground pork
  • 1/2 lb (225 g) ground veal or beef
  • 1 small onion, finely chopped
  • 2 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1/4 cup (25 g) breadcrumbs
  • 1/4 cup (60 ml) whole milk
  • 1 egg
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) butter
  • 1 tablespoon (15 ml) olive oil
  • 1 cup (240 ml) dry cider (Brut cider)
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) chicken or vegetable broth
  • 1 teaspoon fresh thyme leaves
  • 1 tablespoon (15 ml) apple cider vinegar
  • Fresh parsley, chopped (for garnish)

Method

  1. In a small bowl, soak the breadcrumbs in milk and let them absorb for 5 minutes.
  2. In a large bowl, combine ground pork, ground veal or beef, soaked breadcrumbs, chopped onion, minced garlic, egg, salt, and pepper. Mix gently until just combined.
  3. Shape the mixture into small meatballs, about 1 inch (2.5 cm) in diameter.
  4. Heat butter and olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
  5. Add the meatballs in batches and brown them on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Remove and set aside.
  6. In the same skillet, pour in the dry cider and chicken broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
  7. Add thyme and apple cider vinegar, then bring the sauce to a simmer.
  8. Return the meatballs to the skillet, cover, and cook gently for 20 minutes until cooked through and the sauce has thickened slightly.
  9. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
  10. Serve the meatballs hot, garnished with fresh parsley, alongside crusty bread or boiled potatoes.

Tips

  • Use a good quality dry (Brut) cider for authentic flavor.
  • For a richer sauce, finish with a tablespoon of cream just before serving.
  • These meatballs can be made a day ahead and reheated gently in the cider sauce.
